KYC and CDD: CKYC, V-CIP and the KYC state machine

After this lesson you can:
  • Walk the KYC/CDD pipeline: acceptance, identification, verification, risk categorisation
  • Explain CKYC reuse, V-CIP rules and the Aadhaar storage prohibition
  • Describe ongoing due diligence: periodic re-KYC and screening
On this page
  1. Know Your Customer is a pipeline, not a form
  2. The reuse and remote rails: CKYC and V-CIP
  3. KYC never finishes
  4. Where this lives in LoanOS
  5. Knowledge check

1. Know Your Customer is a pipeline, not a form

The KYC Master Direction requires a Customer Acceptance Policy, customer identification via officially valid documents (PAN plus an OVD such as passport, driving licence, Aadhaar-derived documents), verification of those documents, and risk categorisation (low / medium / high) that drives everything downstream — the depth of due diligence, the re-KYC cycle and the monitoring intensity.

Due diligence deepens with risk: beneficial-owner identification for entities, source-of-funds checks for high-risk profiles, PEP (politically exposed person) treatment with senior-management approval.

2. The reuse and remote rails: CKYC and V-CIP

Two rails make KYC scale:

  • CKYC — the central registry. An RE searches by identifier, downloads an existing KYC record with the customer's consent, and uploads new/updated records in the prescribed template. Reuse cuts friction, but the RE remains responsible for currency and accuracy.
  • V-CIP — video-based customer identification: a trained official conducts a live, geo-tagged, liveness-checked video session; the recording and logs are stored in India and the output is approved by an authorised official.

And one hard boundary: Aadhaar biometrics, OTPs and PID blocks are never stored.

Aadhaar-based authentication happens at the boundary service; only the outcome and permitted references persist.

LoanOS enforces this with prohibited-storage checks — it is a test, not a guideline.

3. KYC never finishes

Verification is a state with an expiry, not a milestone.

The direction requires periodic re-KYC on a risk-based cycle (high risk most frequently, low risk least), advance notices to customers, and ongoing screening: PEP lists, UN/UAPA sanctions, internal negative lists — with rescreening when lists refresh.

Transaction monitoring feeds AML alerts, investigations and, where warranted, STR filings to FIU-IND — with strict tipping-off controls so the customer never learns a report was made.

In LoanOS the KYC record is a state machine: verified states carry expiry; an expired or deficient KYC blocks dependent transitions; V-CIP evidence and India-storage attributes are recorded on the record itself.

Regulatory anchors

  • RBI-KYC-2016 — The Master Direction behind CAP, CDD, V-CIP, periodic updation, screening and FIU-IND reporting.
  • UIDAI-AADHAAR — No biometric/OTP/PID persistence; authentication follows UIDAI controls.
  • CERSAI-CKYC — CKYC registry operations: search, download, upload in prescribed templates.

Family IDs resolve in the India regulatory register (docs/compliance/india-regulatory-register.md), which owns sources and caveats.

Where this lives in LoanOS

  • Capability KYC-003 — CKYC search, download, update and upload.
  • Capability KYC-004 — V-CIP evidence, liveness, location and official approval.
  • Capability KYC-005 — Aadhaar boundary with prohibited-data controls.
  • Capability KYC-011 — PEP, UAPA, UN sanctions and internal negative-list screening.
  • Code packages/core/src/compliance-controls.js — KYC verified-state and Aadhaar prohibited-storage checks feeding the preflight.

Key terms

CKYC V-CIP Aadhaar PAN FIU-IND STR

Knowledge check

1. Which of these may LoanOS store after an Aadhaar-based authentication?

  1. The fingerprint template, encrypted
  2. The OTP, hashed
  3. Only the authentication outcome and permitted references
  4. The full PID block for audit
Show answer

C. UIDAI rules prohibit persisting biometrics, OTP and PID in any form; the platform records outcomes and evidence references only.

2. What does risk categorisation drive?

  1. Only the interest rate
  2. Depth of due diligence, re-KYC frequency and monitoring intensity
  3. Branch assignment
  4. Nothing after onboarding
Show answer

B. Low/medium/high categorisation is the dial for the whole ongoing-KYC machine, including periodic updation cycles.
